clue.text: Challenges criminal trials (8)

blocks.note: a con is a convict, a criminal

annotation.surface: Defence lawyers mounting challenges in criminal trials.
annotation.walkthrough: The courtroom surface makes 'criminal trials' look like one phrase; it splits into two pieces, and 'Challenges' is the definition as a noun or verb.
annotation.definitionFit: Both nouns name a clash in which rivals compete, and as verbs both mean disputing a claim, a verdict or a will.

clue.text: Have bagel with starter of nuggets (3)

indicators.note: the starter of a meal comes first, so this takes the first letter

blocks.note: a bagel is ring-shaped, like the letter O
W is the abbreviation for with

annotation.surface: A lunch order: a bagel with some nuggets to start.
annotation.walkthrough: 'With' looks like a joining word but supplies W, as in w/ on a menu, and the bagel gives O by its shape.
annotation.definitionFit: Possession: holding property as yours is having it, a plain synonym.

clue.text: In art institute, son shows discernment (5)

indicators.note: the son goes in the art institute

blocks.note: the Tate, London's national art galleries

annotation.surface: A young man at an art school proves he has a good eye.
annotation.walkthrough: The Tate is the group of British national art galleries, Tate Britain and Tate Modern among them; 'shows' just links wordplay to definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Taste is discernment in judging what is good or fine.

clue.text: Vexed stars possibly desperate for it? (3-7)

indicators.note: the letters of VEXED STARS could possibly be arranged another way

annotation.surface: Frustrated celebrities, perhaps, suffering a certain kind of hunger.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Desperate for it' is a coy euphemism, and the question mark admits it; the vexation of the stars hints at the cause.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone sex-starved is desperate for 'it', the coy word for sex.

clue.text: Bear crossing river in desert (6)

indicators.note: STAND lies across, so goes around, the river

blocks.note: to stand something is to bear it

annotation.surface: A bear wading a river somewhere in the desert.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Desert' reads as a sandy noun, but it is the verb: to leave someone stranded is to desert them.
annotation.definitionFit: To strand someone is to leave them helpless, to desert them.

clue.text: Elder sister? (6)

blocks.note: the surface reads older; the setter means a senior figure in a church
the surface reads a sibling; the setter means a nun, addressed as Sister

annotation.surface: A family member: the older of two sisters.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Elder sister' means the older sibling, but a nun is a sister and an elder is a senior figure in a church, so the head of an abbey fits.
annotation.definitionFit: An abbess heads a community of nuns, each called Sister, so she is their senior.

clue.text: A long way off, Nadal turned up (4)

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up reads the letters bottom to top

blocks.note: Rafa Nadal, the Spanish tennis player

annotation.surface: Nadal appearing at a tournament from far away.
annotation.walkthrough: Rafael Nadal is known as Rafa; reading RAFA upwards gives the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Afar means at or to a great distance.

clue.text: Chief American star in samba style (5,4)

blocks.note: a nova is a star that suddenly brightens

annotation.surface: A leading American star dancing the samba.
annotation.walkthrough: Bossa nova is the Brazilian style that grew out of samba, with a cooler jazz feel.
annotation.definitionFit: Bossa nova is a Brazilian music and dance style derived from samba.

clue.text: Conservative interrupting small bank clerk, one providing an account (11)

indicators.note: TORY breaks into S TELLER

blocks.note: s = small, as on clothing labels
a Tory is a member of the Conservative Party
a teller is a bank clerk

annotation.surface: A Tory politician barging in on a junior bank clerk giving an account of the books.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Account' feels like banking, fitting the teller, but the definition means a story.
annotation.definitionFit: An account here is a narrative; whoever narrates tales or anecdotes supplies one.

clue.text: At heart, pronoun is exceptionally inclusive in terms of gender (6)

indicators.note: the answer sits in the middle of the phrase that follows

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of pronoun through is into the start of exceptionally

annotation.surface: A remark on gender-neutral pronouns as an unusually inclusive choice.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is on-topic: pronouns and gender. The answer runs across three words.
annotation.definitionFit: Unisex means suitable for either sex, so inclusive of both genders.

clue.text: Howard so excited for travelling entertainment (8)

indicators.note: the letters are stirred up

annotation.surface: Someone called Howard thrilled about a touring show.
annotation.walkthrough: Howard is just a name supplying letters; nothing to do with any particular Howard.
annotation.definitionFit: A roadshow is a show that tours from place to place.

clue.text: You said softly, compiling crosswords is distressing (9)

indicators.note: YOU spoken sounds like the letter U

blocks.note: the letter U sounds like you

annotation.surface: Someone telling a crossword setter how painful their job is.
annotation.walkthrough: A setter is the crossword compiler, so compiling crosswords is setting. P is the musical mark for piano, softly.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe events causing someone worry, grief or emotional pain.

clue.text: Numbers of pearls I link clumsily (11)

indicators.note: the letters are handled clumsily, so jumbled

annotation.surface: Someone clumsily stringing a necklace, counting how many pearls.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Numbers' is not counting: it is NUMB-ers, things that numb. It reads as a noun in both senses, plural, so the swap works.
annotation.definitionFit: A 'numb-er' is anything that deadens feeling, which is exactly what analgesic drugs do.

clue.text: Stray cuckoo for lecherous woodland god (5)

indicators.note: cuckoo means crazy, so the letters go wild

annotation.surface: A stray cuckoo fluttering around a randy forest deity.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cuckoo' fits the woodland scene as a bird but works as the adjective crazy.
annotation.definitionFit: A satyr is a Greek woodland god, part goat, famous for lust.

clue.text: Hero sent in rocks – this is a fake rock (10)

indicators.note: the letters are rocked, shaken about

annotation.surface: A hero thrown onto the rocks, and the gem he finds is fake.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rocks' wants to be stones, matching the definition, but it is the verb: the fodder rocks. The definition's 'rock' is slang for a gem.
annotation.definitionFit: A rhinestone is an imitation diamond, and a diamond is a rock in slang.

clue.text: Pay no attention to Signora with no clothing and energy (6)

indicators.note: strip off the outer letters, the word's clothes

blocks.note: SIGNORA without its outer S and A

annotation.surface: Trying to look away from an Italian lady who has nothing on.
annotation.walkthrough: Signora is Italian for Mrs or madam; undressing a word removes its first and last letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean deliberately disregarding someone or something.

clue.text: He and I intent to organise important birthday (9)

indicators.note: arrange the letters into a new order

annotation.surface: Two people planning a big birthday party.
annotation.walkthrough: 'And' only strings He and I together; the fodder is HE, I and INTENT. A ninetieth is a milestone birthday, so it counts as important.
annotation.definitionFit: Birthdays ending in zero are celebrated as milestones, and reaching age ninety is a big occasion.

clue.text: Letters seen on taps with capital kind of metal (6)

blocks.note: C and H, marking cold and hot taps

annotation.surface: Describing fancy chrome-plated taps.
annotation.walkthrough: British basins often have separate hot and cold taps marked H and C; the answer fits the scene, since taps are often chrome.
annotation.definitionFit: Chrome is chromium, or chromium plating, a metal.

clue.text: Barbie’s beau regularly unveils pet shelter (6)

indicators.note: take letters at regular intervals: every second one

annotation.surface: Barbie's boyfriend Ken opening a new animal shelter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Unveils' reads like an opening ceremony, but only its alternate letters count.
annotation.definitionFit: A kennel is a small hut where a dog sleeps or boarding dogs stay, so it houses animals.

clue.text: Involve English translation of Latin (6)

indicators.note: translating changes the form of LATIN, so its letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A classroom task that requires putting Latin into English.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a school translation exercise; 'translation' here is a signal to rearrange, not to translate.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: when one thing necessarily brings another with it, it requires or includes it.

clue.text: Expects disastrous Tory PM to admit fault, ultimately (6)

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so TRUSS lets the T inside it
ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of fault is taken

blocks.note: Liz Truss, Conservative prime minister for 49 days in 2022

annotation.surface: Hoping a failed prime minister will finally own up to her mistakes.
annotation.walkthrough: Liz Truss was the British Conservative prime minister whose 2022 term collapsed within weeks. 'Disastrous' describes her, not an anagram: TRUS(T)S.
annotation.definitionFit: To trust that something will happen is to expect it.

clue.text: Loud old stringed instrument or wind instrument (5)

blocks.note: the lute, a plucked Renaissance instrument

annotation.surface: Choosing between a noisy antique lute and a wind instrument.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Or' offers a choice on the surface but merely joins wordplay to definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Sounded by blowing across a hole, it belongs to the woodwind section of an orchestra.

clue.text: Metal that is extremely rare making a pair of cups? (9)

indicators.note: take the extremes, the first and last letters, of rare

blocks.note: brass, an alloy of copper and zinc
i.e., Latin id est, that is

annotation.surface: Metal so rare it goes into making a pair of trophy cups.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A pair of cups' suggests trophies or crockery; the question mark flags the other cups.
annotation.definitionFit: The garment is a bra, sold by cup size, so its two halves are literally called cups.

clue.text: Urge that is gripping politician on left (5)

indicators.note: to grip something is to hold it tight, so IE holds MP between its letters
in a down entry, L goes on under the rest

annotation.surface: A call for a left-wing politician to be pressed into action.
annotation.walkthrough: I(MP)E then L.
annotation.definitionFit: To impel is to urge or drive someone to act.

clue.text: Topless fan in part of cricket match (4)

indicators.note: in a down entry the top is the first letter, so remove it

annotation.surface: A shirtless supporter at a cricket match.
annotation.walkthrough: A lover is a fan (a music lover). An over is a set of six balls bowled from one end in cricket.
annotation.definitionFit: An over is a unit of play in cricket: six deliveries by one bowler.

clue.text: Books dealing with what waiter or tennis player does (8)

blocks.clueFragment: what waiter or tennis player does

annotation.surface: A catalogue of books about restaurant staff and tennis.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Books' is the verb, as in booking a table, which the waiter nearly gives away.
annotation.definitionFit: To book a table or seat is to reserve it.

clue.text: Disapprove of affected behaviour after work (6)

indicators.note: after means later in sequence, so POSE is placed behind OP

annotation.surface: Frowning on colleagues who put on airs after hours.
annotation.walkthrough: OP is short for opus, a numbered musical work.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: standing against a plan means objecting to it.

clue.text: Wrong function for a mathematician (3)

blocks.note: the trigonometric function sine, in its written short form

annotation.surface: A mathematician applying the wrong function.
annotation.walkthrough: The sine function is written sin x in trigonometry.
annotation.definitionFit: A moral transgression is a wrong; in trigonometry the sine function is abbreviated to three letters.

clue.text: That lady following Parisian is a Persian queen (6)

indicators.note: following means coming behind, so HER is placed after EST

annotation.surface: A French woman's companion turns out to be royalty from Persia.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Is' belongs to 'Parisian': a Parisian says est. Esther is the Jewish queen of the Persian king in the Book of Esther.
annotation.definitionFit: Esther became queen to the Persian king Ahasuerus in the Bible.

clue.text: Growing roses well in greenhouse? Not entirely (8)

indicators.note: the answer lies in the words
only part of the phrase is used

blocks.note: the letters start at the last letter of roses and end at the first of greenhouse

annotation.surface: Asking whether roses thrive under glass, with a doubtful reply.
annotation.walkthrough: The gardening scene makes 'Growing' look like the topic; it is the definition as an adjective.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe something getting bigger or expanding in size.
